In one sentence: manage an organization's IT and technical teams. The work includes setting plans and budgets, building teams, implementing systems, overseeing security and compliance, coordinating business requirements, and managing vendors and outsourced delivery.

Computer and information systems managers focus on IT strategy, delivery, and accountability. Executive roles emphasize broader business decisions, research roles emphasize discovery, and support roles emphasize process execution. The differences lie in deliverables and responsibility boundaries, not a simple reporting hierarchy.

AI will not replace the occupation as a whole. It absorbs many structured IT tasks, but people retain real-world judgment, final accountability, and interpersonal coordination. The role's resilience comes from technical depth and decision quality (AI exposure 8/10).

Most Computer and information systems manager roles require a bachelor's degree or professional qualification. Career changers can connect prior experience to IT work and enter through assistant or project roles. Education is not the only path; professional ability and demonstrated cases carry greater weight.

A good fit for people with solid expertise, care for detail, the ability to judge under uncertainty, and a habit of continuous learning. Approach with caution if you avoid accountability, dislike repetitive process work, or resist updating your methods.

Computer and information systems managers work across core industries, related services, public organizations, and emerging interdisciplinary fields.
